limits: One same-machine noninteractive integration probe of the current uncommitted fix; not a native office-task run or a performance benchmark.
Direct and recorder readings use the same OS counter interface through psutil; these are cross-checks, not an independent external auditor.
No PID reuse was forced in this integration probe. Controlled regression tests cover reuse and access races separately.
CPU deltas cover first-to-last successful observations. Sampling can miss short-lived processes and memory peaks.
Existing application processes are a warm, nonexclusive cohort. Stability checks cover only identities readable before and after the probe.
Chrome, Notepad and Explorer were not intentionally launched, closed or restarted. Only the owned temporary Python workload was launched; unrelated background activity was not isolated.
No claim of CPU, memory, task-speed or score improvement follows from this probe.

prior_probe.reason: The initial probe selected the Windows virtual-environment launcher PID instead of its actual worker descendant. Its workload assertions failed; the recorder had correctly captured both identities. The corrected probe validates exact worker membership in the owned launcher tree before collecting comparison readings.

validation_scope: Nineteen bounded checks against actual Windows counters with one owned Python workload and existing warm applications; no desktop office task was executed.
